complexity_rationale: Post-PR-001 customer-only scope: 30 contract surfaces (24 customer endpoints + 6 cross-cutting). Sole owner of cookie<->Bearer translation per cross-cutting.auth.token_acquisition_flow (6-step withAuth orchestrator); sole owner of customer-facing Idempotency-Key generation/persistence (UUID v4 per checkout-commit click + in-flight Map debounce). Mobile-first Thai UX with 13 routes (5 bottom-tab + 8 full-screen) shaped by the ShopPilot Frontend Spec; visual system, IA, color tokens, typography lifted from the standalone HTML mockup but reimplemented as Next.js 14 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. A defect in route-handler auth, idempotency wiring, accidental document.cookie usage, or accidental INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET leakage blocks every functional Customer AC.

route_handlers.downstream_contract: probeSession (local; reads access cookie, returns claims if valid; NO refresh side-effect)
route_handlers.purpose: Used by (full)/(tabs) layouts and SessionContext to determine auth UI state without burning a refresh round-trip.

route_handlers.auth_flow: public; on 200 set access+refresh HttpOnly cookies with locked attributes; response body strips raw tokens (returns user object only)
route_handlers.purpose: Login endpoint; cookies are the only auth surface

route_handlers.auth_flow: public; on success do NOT set cookies (registration does not auto-login per BA AUTH-001 — caller hits /login next)
Read 'refresh' cookie -> POST identity.refresh; on 200 rotate both cookies; on AUTH_REVOKED clear both cookies and return 401 AUTH_REVOKED
route_handlers.purpose: Explicit refresh path (rare; standard refresh is implicit inside withAuth wrapping every protected handler)

route_handlers.auth_flow: Read 'refresh' cookie -> POST identity.logout {refreshToken}; ALWAYS clear both cookies (Max-Age=0) regardless of downstream outcome
public passthrough; if access cookie present forward Bearer (no behavior change for catalog list)

route_handlers.notes: Dedicated handler so we can attach a per-request trace correlation header.

route_handlers.client_idempotency_key: REQUIRED. Client (browser) generates a UUID v4 via crypto.randomUUID() per logical Place-Order click; route handler reads it from the request body field 'idempotencyKey' and forwards as 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header to checkout.commit. The handler MUST reject (400 VALIDATION_ERROR) requests missing the field — never auto-generate server-side.
route_handlers.notes: On 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT: handler returns the envelope verbatim with Retry-After echoed; client retries once after 1s. On 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED: handler surfaces the original orderId in envelope.data and the client navigates to /orders/[orderId] WITHOUT creating a new order.
Customer-facing mock screen; outcome is one of SUCCESS|FAILED|TIMEOUT (request body field 'outcome').

route_handler_topology.generic_proxy: POST /api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts handles the remaining 17 customer endpoints (identity.profile.* + identity.address.* + catalog.product.* + catalog.category.list + cart.* + order.list-mine + order.detail + order.cancel-mine). Generic handler reads the rest segments, maps the first segment ('identity'|'catalog'|'cart'|'order') to the matching BACKEND_*_BASE_URL env var, applies withAuth (or public passthrough for catalog), forwards body verbatim, returns envelope verbatim.
route_handler_topology.explicit_route_files: The 'method_path' rows above with /api/proxy/<svc>/<aggregate>/<action> are implemented BY the generic [...path] handler; we list them for traceability rather than as separate route.ts files. ONLY the 8 dedicated rows have their own route.ts.
route_handler_topology.rationale: Keep the surface lean: cookie semantics + Idempotency-Key wiring + observability headers must live in dedicated handlers. Everything else is a stateless POST forward and benefits from a single tested path.

idempotency_strategy.generator: crypto.randomUUID() — UUID v4. Never timestamp, counter, or user-data-derived.
idempotency_strategy.scope: ONE key per (user, Place-Order click). A second click of the Place-Order button generates a NEW key (a new logical attempt).
idempotency_strategy.in_flight_dedup: CheckoutCommitButton holds a Map<'checkout-commit', Promise> in lib/idempotency.ts (InFlightMap). While one attempt is unresolved: (a) the button is disabled, (b) any duplicate click is dropped client-side. This prevents accidental double-submit without minting a new key.
idempotency_strategy.persistence: Held in React state in CheckoutCommitButton ONLY. NOT persisted to localStorage. If the user refreshes mid-submit, a fresh key is generated on the next click; the previously-submitted orderId is what survives — via the URL the user is redirected to (/checkout/payment?orderId=...).
idempotency_strategy.header_forwarding: Client POSTs body { idempotencyKey, ...other } to /api/checkout/commit. The route handler reads idempotencyKey, forwards as 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header on the downstream POST to checkout.commit. Body-field carriage chosen over client-set HTTP header because (a) auditable in handler logs, (b) avoids any future cross-origin preflight concern.
idempotency_strategy.rejection_path: Route handler rejects with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (code surfaced as 'VALIDATION_ERROR') if the body lacks idempotencyKey. The handler MUST NOT auto-generate one — auto-generation defeats replay-safety on user re-submit.

409_handling.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT: Wait Retry-After (default 1s); retry once with the SAME body (same key). If still INFLIGHT, surface a soft toast 'กำลังประมวลผล…' and stop.
409_handling.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED: Read envelope.data.orderId (per checkout.commit failure_modes); router.push(`/orders/${orderId}`); show toast 'คำสั่งซื้อนี้ถูกสร้างไว้แล้ว'. Do NOT retry.

state_management.approach: Server Components by default for read-once pages (home, search shell, detail, orders, orderDetail, orderSuccess, orderResult, profile). 'use client' ONLY where interactivity is required: cart line controls, search filters, login/register form, address form, addresses page, checkout summary+commit button, payment simulate buttons, logout button, cancel-order button.
state_management.context_usage: React Context exclusively for auth-derived state (SessionContext: {authenticated, user}). Populated once per top-level navigation by /api/auth/session probe in the layout; child Client Components either consume via useSessionContext() or re-fetch on demand.
state_management.no_redux: No Redux. No Zustand. No SWR. No React Query. The cookie holds the JWT; cart and order state are server-truth via cart.read / order.list-mine / order.detail. This keeps the dependency surface small for MVP.
state_management.data_fetching: Server Components: native fetch with revalidate:0 (cookie-bearing requests are dynamic by definition). Client Components: native fetch + useState/useEffect; AbortController on unmount.
state_management.rationale: Cart state living server-side prevents drift with backend stock/price changes. Cookie holds JWT; the session probe makes user identity available to the layout server-side; child Client Components either receive it via SessionContext or re-fetch /api/auth/session on demand (negligible cost, in-memory probe).

cookies.attributes_production: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age = matching token expiry (access 15min, refresh 14d)
cookies.attributes_local_dev: Same as production but Secure flag OMITTED on http://localhost (browsers reject Secure on insecure origins). Driven by NODE_ENV.
cookies.rotation: On every successful identity.refresh both cookies are re-set with rotated values (Set-Cookie x2).
cookies.clearance: On AUTH_REVOKED (refresh-rejected) and on /api/auth/logout, both cookies are cleared via Set-Cookie name=; Max-Age=0; same Path.

security_posture.no_javascript_jwt: Lint rule bans document.cookie reads outside lib/auth.ts (custom ESLint regex); HttpOnly attribute prevents JS read anyway. No code path serializes JWT into HTML or NEXT_PUBLIC_* env. CSP connect-src 'self' prevents JS exfiltration via fetch.
security_posture.no_internal_secret: REV-L2-013: frontend/.env.example explicitly OMITS INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET. Route handlers NEVER set X-Internal-Secret. A regression test asserts (a) the env var is undefined at runtime and (b) no outgoing fetch from the frontend runtime carries an X-Internal-Secret header (Playwright network interception in CI).
security_posture.xss: React default escaping. dangerouslySetInnerHTML is FORBIDDEN repo-wide (eslint rule react/no-danger=error). User-supplied product description rendered as plain text only.
security_posture.csrf: SameSite=Lax on both cookies neutralizes cross-site form submissions. All mutating route handlers require Content-Type: application/json (rejects form-urlencoded), blocking naive HTML-form CSRF. Same-origin POST from our SPA carries cookies as expected.

csp_headers_baseline_next_config.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'

security_posture.csp_no_unsafe_eval: 'unsafe-eval' is NOT included in script-src. 'unsafe-inline' for script-src is a known Next.js App Router constraint pre-nonce-middleware; tracked as a follow-up to add per-request nonces. Style 'unsafe-inline' stays for Tailwind JIT injected styles.
security_posture.input_size_limits: Route handlers cap body size at 1 MB via Next.js route segment config (custom JSON body-parser limit) to mitigate DoS.
security_posture.secrets: All BACKEND_*_BASE_URL env vars are server-only (no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix). They are referenced inside route handlers (server runtime) and never bundled into client JS.

error_handling.envelope_unwrap: lib/http.ts unwraps {code, message, data, traceId}. Success codes (SUCCESS, CREATED) return data; non-success throw an ApiError carrying {code, message, traceId, http}.

primary_journey_§7_1_spine: Spine: register -> login -> browse / -> filter on /search by category -> open /detail/[id] -> add to cart -> /cart shows server subtotal -> /checkout pick default address -> see server subtotal+shippingFee+grandTotal -> Place Order (asserts Idempotency-Key header on intercepted downstream request) -> /checkout/payment click 'สำเร็จ' -> /checkout/orderSuccess -> /orders/[id] shows status='ชำระเงินแล้ว' with PENDING_PAYMENT and PAID rows in the timeline
additional_scenarios: Payment FAILED: same up to /checkout/payment; click 'ไม่สำเร็จ' -> /checkout/orderResult; /orders/[id] shows status='ชำระเงินไม่สำเร็จ'
Payment TIMEOUT: same; click 'หมดเวลา' -> /checkout/orderResult; /orders/[id] shows status='หมดเวลาชำระเงิน'
Idempotency replay: intercept first commit, re-submit form with the same idempotencyKey body field -> assert single orderId and a 200 envelope (proves CHK-009 client-side wiring)
Re-click Place Order rapidly: only one network call leaves the browser (in-flight de-dup); if forced second click is allowed, a NEW UUID is sent (proves 'one key per click')
Auth refresh: log in, fast-forward access cookie expiry (set Max-Age=1, wait), navigate to /orders -> route handler refreshes cookies transparently AND no re-login is required (AUTH-005)
AUTH_REVOKED: tamper refresh cookie -> next protected nav 307-redirects to /login and both cookies are cleared
Auth deep-link resume: open /orders/[id] unauthenticated -> redirected to /login?next=%2Forders%2F<id>; on login success router.push(next) takes the customer back to the original orderDetail
Pricing boundary: cart subtotal=1499 -> shippingFee=฿60 grandTotal=฿1,559; subtotal=1500 -> shippingFee=฿0 grandTotal=฿1,500 (Frontend Spec §5 + §11.2)
Cart non-checkoutable flag: seed an INACTIVE product in cart -> /cart shows 'ไม่สามารถสั่งซื้อได้' badge AND 'ดำเนินการชำระเงิน' button is disabled (CART-005)
Soft-delete snapshot: admin soft-deletes a product (via curl) -> /products list excludes it AND /orders/[id] historical row still renders snapshot fields (CAT-009 / ORD-007)
Cancel pending: customer cancels a PENDING_PAYMENT order -> status flips to CANCELLED; cancel button hides (ORD-004)
Mobile viewport: every route renders at 390x844 without horizontal scroll AND reflows down to 360 (matchMedia in Playwright)
Thai-only assertions: every page declares lang='th'; ฿ prefix appears wherever an amount is rendered; emerald (#1a8060) computed-style on every primary CTA
No-internal-secret regression: Playwright network-interception asserts no outgoing request from the frontend runtime carries 'X-Internal-Secret' header (REV-L2-013 verified-correct posture)
integration.fixtures: Playwright runs against the docker-compose stack (7 backends + frontend). Test data seeded via direct backend POSTs in a globalSetup (no admin UI exists).

test_strategy.lint_and_static: ESLint with next/core-web-vitals + react/no-danger=error + custom rule banning document.cookie reads outside lib/auth.ts. TypeScript strict mode (no implicit any, no unchecked indexed access).

observability.trace_propagation: Route handlers read incoming traceparent (W3C) header from the browser if present and forward it to backend POSTs as 'traceparent' header. If absent, generate one (crypto.randomUUID-derived) so backend logs correlate.
observability.client_logging: console.error on ApiError with traceId; production builds have console.log/info stripped via Next.js compiler removeConsole option (keep error/warn).
observability.no_pii_in_logs: Email/phone/address never logged on the client; only userId (UUID) and traceId.

open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.issue: Payment route convention path: cross-cutting.route-convention.examples.payment lists 'POST /api/v1/payment/intent/simulate' (intent aggregate). frontend handler /api/payment/simulate must hard-code that downstream URL. Same pattern for payment.intent.callback (server-to-server only; not a frontend concern).
open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.frontend_assumption: Use POST {BACKEND_PAYMENT_BASE_URL}/api/v1/payment/intent/simulate per route-convention.examples.payment[1]. No frontend behavior change needed; documented for traceability.

open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.issue: checkout.commit Idempotency-Key transport (header vs body): contract specifies 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header. Browsers can set custom headers on same-origin fetch without preflight, so the client could send the header directly. We choose body-field carriage ({idempotencyKey}) and let the route handler map to the downstream HTTP header — for auditability and to eliminate any future cross-origin preflight concern. Backend contract is unaffected.
open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.frontend_assumption: Client sends UUID v4 in body field 'idempotencyKey'; handler maps to downstream 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header. Tech-Lead: flag if body-field convention is unacceptable; switch to header-direct is one-line.

open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.issue: GET /api/auth/session is the only GET handler in our surface. cross-cutting.route-convention.trailing_rules says 'GET reserved for /liveness, /readiness, /metrics' on backend services; frontend route handlers are NOT backend services and the convention does not bind them. We use GET because the session probe is a pure read with no body.
open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.frontend_assumption: GET /api/auth/session is approved frontend-side (Cache-Control: no-store still applied). If Tech-Lead wants strict POST-everywhere even on frontend route handlers, switch is one-line.

open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.issue: Frontend Spec §3 lists a 'review' route for star-rating + comment on an orderDetail item. EPIC_FRONTEND.out_of_scope[1] explicitly defers the review module. We ship a placeholder route file at /orders/[orderId]/review/[itemId] that renders a Thai 'เร็ว ๆ นี้' message so deep links don't 404, but no behavior is wired. The 13 routes count in this spec is the post-defer count and matches Frontend Spec §3 minus the deferred review row count.
open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.frontend_assumption: Routes table sticks to the 13-row deliverable per the prompt; placeholder file exists for graceful 200 on deep link. No AC depends on it.

open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.issue: Buddhist-era date formatting: ADR-010 mentions Buddhist-era 'where date is rendered to the customer' but no story AC specifies it. We default to Intl.DateTimeFormat('th-TH-u-ca-buddhist') for orders/orderDetail timestamps. If Tech-Lead prefers Gregorian, switch via lib/format.ts is trivial.
open_contract_ambiguities_surfaced_to_te.frontend_assumption: Buddhist-era for customer-visible timestamps; ISO-8601 UTC remains the underlying API value.
